operations.details_summary: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m current official source revalidated on 2026-07-24.

Covers approximately 99% of England at 1 m spatial resolution. | Heights are in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and use OSTN15. | Input LIDAR surveys have vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE. | The dataset is Open Government Licence and is updated annually.
Source role is constrained to its documented resolution, accuracy, datum and publication semantics; no higher-precision claim is inferred.

The plus or minus 15 cm RMSE is a source-survey vertical accuracy statement, not a parcel-specific 95% confidence interval. | Composite cells can originate from surveys of different dates; survey-lineage metadata is required for time-sensitive interpretation.

Parcel evidence remains admissible only with exact canonical row, exact HMLR INSPIRE polygon and point-in-polygon, EA 1 m primary sample, 2 m crosscheck, datum/lineage disclosure and hash-backed source evidence.
LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 2m current official source revalidated on 2026-07-24.

The 2 m composite is an official Environment Agency DTM product. | Heights are in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and use OSTN15. | Input LIDAR surveys have vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
Source role is constrained to its documented resolution, accuracy, datum and publication semantics; no higher-precision claim is inferred.

The 2 m product is retained as an independent resolution crosscheck and does not replace the 1 m primary parcel measurement. | Agreement between 1 m and 2 m products does not eliminate shared source-survey errors.

Parcel evidence remains admissible only with exact canonical row, exact HMLR INSPIRE polygon and point-in-polygon, EA 1 m primary sample, 2 m crosscheck, datum/lineage disclosure and hash-backed source evidence.
INSPIRE Index Polygons spatial data current official source revalidated on 2026-07-24.

The dataset shows the indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties in England and Wales. | The current download page states the dataset was published on 5 July 2026. | New files are published on the first Sunday of every month and downloads are available by local authority. | Downloads are provided under Open Government Licence conditions.
Source role is constrained to its documented resolution, accuracy, datum and publication semantics; no higher-precision claim is inferred.

INSPIRE Index Polygons are indicative spatial extents and are not a legal title-boundary determination. | A parcel result is accepted only when the exact HMLR INSPIRE identifier and point-in-polygon gate both pass.

Parcel evidence remains admissible only with exact canonical row, exact HMLR INSPIRE polygon and point-in-polygon, EA 1 m primary sample, 2 m crosscheck, datum/lineage disclosure and hash-backed source evidence.
OS Terrain 50 Overview current official source revalidated on 2026-07-24.

OS Terrain 50 is a 50 m post-spacing digital terrain model with full Great Britain coverage. | The product is OS OpenData and is updated annually in July. | OS Terrain 50 grid heights have been verified to 4 m RMSE.
Source role is constrained to its documented resolution, accuracy, datum and publication semantics; no higher-precision claim is inferred.

At 50 m spacing and 4 m RMSE, OS Terrain 50 is unsuitable as the primary source for sub-metre parcel height-difference measurement. | It is retained only as a coarse terrain sanity and gross-outlier crosscheck.

Parcel evidence remains admissible only with exact canonical row, exact HMLR INSPIRE polygon and point-in-polygon, EA 1 m primary sample, 2 m crosscheck, datum/lineage disclosure and hash-backed source evidence.
National Geoid Model OSGM15 current official source revalidated on 2026-07-24.

OSGM15 converts ETRS89 ellipsoid height to orthometric height and provides ODN heights on mainland Britain. | The model uses a 1 km grid with bilinear interpolation. | Nominal geoid-model accuracy is 8 mm RMS in mainland UK.
Source role is constrained to its documented resolution, accuracy, datum and publication semantics; no higher-precision claim is inferred.

OSGM15 transformation accuracy does not replace the elevation-source accuracy budget. | Datum transformation evidence must remain separate from terrain-surface variation and raster sampling uncertainty.

Parcel evidence remains admissible only with exact canonical row, exact HMLR INSPIRE polygon and point-in-polygon, EA 1 m primary sample, 2 m crosscheck, datum/lineage disclosure and hash-backed source evidence.
LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles current official source revalidated on 2026-07-24.

The time-stamped archive contains Environment Agency DTM surveys at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m resolution depending on survey. | Heights are in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid. | The dataset states vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE. | The metadata catalogue identifies survey date, product resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
Source role is constrained to its documented resolution, accuracy, datum and publication semantics; no higher-precision claim is inferred.

Historical tiles may use transformation/geoid models specific to their survey period and must not be silently mixed with current composite values. | Historical data is lineage evidence unless an explicit dated comparison is requested and datum handling is disclosed.

Parcel evidence remains admissible only with exact canonical row, exact HMLR INSPIRE polygon and point-in-polygon, EA 1 m primary sample, 2 m crosscheck, datum/lineage disclosure and hash-backed source evidence.
